<reflection>
After three experiments, the cumulative negative log-likelihood (NLL) values show that M5, M3, and M4 are the best-fitting mechanisms, but many others remain within a few NLL units, indicating continued ambiguity. The third experiment (doubling catalyst) increased the spread of NLLs, with M5, M3, and M4 pulling ahead, but a large group of mechanisms (M6, M8, M12, etc.) still have non-negligible support. The aim of the third experiment to probe catalyst dependence was achieved, but further discrimination is needed. Notably, M20 is consistently the worst fit and can likely be deprioritized.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Proposing an experiment with low substrate concentration (0.5 M) while keeping catalyst at 0.01 M and product at 0. This design explores a new regime where substrate is only moderately in excess relative to catalyst, contrasting with previous high-substrate conditions. This will be sensitive to saturation effects, substrate inhibition, and substrate-dependent steps across many mechanisms. For example: mechanisms with Michaelis-Menten kinetics (M1, M2) will show different apparent saturation; mechanisms with substrate inhibition (M7, M16) may exhibit reduced rates at high substrate but not at low substrate; mechanisms with substrate-induced deactivation (M11) may show different deactivation profiles; and mechanisms involving substrate binding to multiple catalyst species (M3, M5, M19) may display distinct concentration dependencies. By comparing kinetics at low vs. high substrate, we can constrain these aspects simultaneously for a wide range of mechanisms, enhancing discrimination without resorting to extreme conditions that might obscure differences.
</hypothesis>
